parts.label: (a)(i)
key_concepts: power as rate of work done
hints: Hint 1: Think about what makes a powerful engine different - is it just how much work it can do, or how quickly it can do that work?
parts.proper_answer: Power is the work done per unit time (rate of energy transfer).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What Power Really Means**
Power tells you how fast work is being done. Two identical lorries might do the same work climbing a hill, but the one that does it in less time is more powerful. So you always link work to time.

Step 2: **Exact Definition**
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$ In words: power is work done per unit time, measured in watts ($\text{W}$) where $1\text{ W} = 1\text{ J s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Start by recalling how work done is linked to the force in the direction of motion and the distance moved along that direction.
Hint 2: Now think how power brings time into this, and what distance divided by time represents for steady motion.
parts.proper_answer: $W = Fs$ and $P = W/t$, so $P = Fs/t = Fv$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Work Done by a Steady Force**
Imagine pushing with a constant force $F$ in the direction you move through a distance $s$. The work you do is:
$$W = Fs$$

Step 2: **Bring in Power**
Power is how fast that work is done:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$
Substitute $W$ from Step 1:
$$P = \frac{Fs}{t}$$

Step 3: **Spot the Velocity**
For motion at steady speed, distance per unit time is velocity:
$$v = \frac{s}{t}$$
So:
$$P = F \times \frac{s}{t} = Fv$$ This only applies when $F$ and $v$ are parallel.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: For steady speed on the flat, the forward driving force must exactly balance the resistive force. Consider how power, driving force and speed are connected, and first convert 130 kW to watts.
parts.proper_answer: $F = P/v = 130 \times 10^3 / 25 = 5200\text{ N}$. At constant speed driving force = resistive force, so resistive force = $5200\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Steady Speed Means Balanced Forces**
On a horizontal road at constant $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ there is no acceleration, so resultant force is zero. That means:
forward driving force = backward resistive force.

Step 2: **Use Power to Find the Force**
$$P = Fv$$
Rearrange before putting numbers in:
$$F = \frac{P}{v}$$
Convert: $P = 130\text{ kW} = 130 \times 10^3\text{ W}$.
$$F = \frac{130 \times 10^3}{25} = 5200\text{ N}$$
So the resistive force is also $5200\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Weight always acts vertically down with size mg. Picture resolving it into two parts relative to the slope - which trigonometric function gives the part pulling the lorry back down the slope?
parts.proper_answer: Component parallel to slope $= mg \sin\theta$ down the slope.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Resolve the Weight**
Weight $mg$ acts straight down, but the slope is tilted by $\theta$. Resolve $mg$ into components perpendicular to the road and parallel to the road.

Step 2: **Parallel Component**
By right-angled triangle geometry, the angle between $mg$ and the perpendicular to the slope is also $\theta$. The side opposite that angle is the downhill component:
$$F_{parallel} = mg \sin\theta$$
This acts down the slope, opposing the uphill motion.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: At constant speed uphill, think about all the forces pulling back down the slope that the engine must now overcome.
Hint 2: Calculate the extra downhill pull due to weight using m = 36000 kg, g = 9.81 m s-2 and theta = 1.4 degrees.
Hint 3: Add this to the 5200 N resistive force to get the total driving force, then link that total force to power at 25 m s-1.
parts.proper_answer: Weight component $= 36000 \times 9.81 \times \sin 1.4^{\circ} \approx 8630\text{ N}$. Total $F = 5200 + 8630 = 13830\text{ N}$. $P = Fv = 13830 \times 25 \approx 350 \times 10^3\text{ W} = 350\text{ kW}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Forces Needed for Steady Speed Uphill**
Constant speed means no resultant force. The engine must now push uphill against two things: the 5200 N resistive force plus the component of weight down the slope.

Step 2: **Calculate the Weight Component**
$$F_{weight} = mg \sin\theta$$
$$F_{weight} = 36000 \times 9.81 \times \sin 1.4^{\circ}$$
$$F_{weight} \approx 8630\text{ N}$$
This is larger than the air and rolling resistance.

Step 3: **Total Driving Force and Power**
Total forward force needed:
$$F_{total} = 5200 + 8630 \approx 13800\text{ N}$$
Power at $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = F_{total}v$$
$$P \approx 13800 \times 25 \approx 3.5 \times 10^5\text{ W} = 350\text{ kW}$$
